s4_s6.finding: All four corrected 2026-10-03 S4->S6 raw confusions are won by the same legacy S6 asset. Direct pixel review shows that asset contains adjacent-tile remnants instead of a clean single-tile face.

leave_source_session_out.changed_prediction_note: Two held-out S4 queries remain wrong but move from S6 to other low-confidence wrong classes; total LOSO correctness is unchanged.
leave_source_session_out.interpretation: storage-session regression only, never independent original-match promotion evidence

global_legacy_removal_rejected.reason: Removing every non-tile_* legacy asset is too broad. M4 and S3 have no modern tile_* concealed support, so a global legacy purge can create new coverage failures even though some aggregate development metrics improve.

s4_s6.decision: Keep this exact S6 asset as a quarantine candidate only. Do not mutate Runtime labels until a new source-disjoint batch confirms no regression.

m2_m3.finding: The three remaining corrected M2 queries are a true cross-render-domain classification problem, not a truth-label defect or a threshold problem.

pending_20261003_reviewed_m2_crop.note: Even this same-match reviewed M2 crop does not outrank the M3 winner on the three revealed queries. Syncing it may improve support provenance but is not by itself an identity fix.

brightness_threshold_probe.decision: reject; it trades away too much accepted coverage and still does not fix M2

m2_m3.decision: Do not lower 0.82 and do not add an M2-specific heuristic. Treat M2/M3 as a cross-domain representation/data-diversity problem. Prefer a source-grouped learned candidate or genuinely diverse reviewed M2 sources, evaluated on a different original match.

next_step: Keep the exact S6 quarantine candidate offline until a new source-disjoint whole-hand batch is available.
